outcome: Acid-base balance at birth (cord pH, BE, HCO3)
cohort: 120 newborns from mothers with diabetes and 120 controls from uncomplicated pregnancies, in a specialized tertiary center over a period of 4 years
finding: Newborns of diabetic mothers, despite having similar acid-base balance at birth compared to controls, had a significantly higher rate of Cesarean delivery, indicating a need for intensive monitoring and care for potential complications like hypoglycemia.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the predominant mode of delivery in the diabetic group (4 out of every 5 cases).
